El Salvador’s Bukele Declares War on Haiti’s Gangs. Donroe Doctrine in Play? The man who crushed El Salvador’s gangs has taken his war abroad.
More than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers are now in Haiti, a country where gangs control most of the capital, more than 1.5 million people have fled their homes, and there has been no president since 2021. The trigger was an ambush on 18 October that left four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing. When an aid group handed over four bodies, Bukele rejected them: “Not our men.”
